function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Here’s a quick rundown of places you can order a cake from—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or just a convenient delivery option.

| Option | What it offers | How to get it | Tips |
|--------|----------------|---------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; great for supporting small businesses | Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Yelp; call ahead | Call to confirm availability & delivery hours; many accept online orders via their website or Facebook page |
| **Specialty cake shops** | Signature flavors, themed designs, premium ingredients | Look up “custom cake shop” + your city; many have Instagram pages showcasing past work | Send photos of your design idea; ask about dietary options (gluten‑free, vegan, sugar‑free) |
| **Grocery store chains** | In‑store bakeries + online ordering (e.g., Walmart, Kroger, Safeway) | Order through the store’s app or website; pick‑up or delivery | Check for same‑day delivery windows; some offer “pick‑up at the bakery” for fresher options |
| **Online marketplaces** | Wide variety of local bakers & national brands (Etsy, Goldbelly) | Browse categories (“birthday cakes,” “wedding cakes”) | Read seller ratings; shipping may add extra cost/time |
| **Food‑delivery apps** | Quick delivery from restaurants & bakeries (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates) | Search “cakes” or “desserts” in the app; filter by rating | Delivery fees apply; check for “special instructions” field for dietary needs |
| **Subscription boxes** | Monthly cake deliveries (e.g., Cake of the Month Club) | Sign up on the company’s website | Great for recurring celebrations; usually includes recipe cards |
| **Amazon Fresh / Instacart** | Grocery pickup/delivery that includes pre‑baked cakes | Add a cake to your cart; schedule delivery | Good for last‑minute needs; check for “freshness guarantee” |

### How to choose the right place

1. **Know your budget** – Local bakeries can range from $20–$100+ depending on size & customization. Online marketplaces often list prices upfront.
2. **Check dietary restrictions** – If you need gluten‑free, vegan, or allergy‑friendly options, look for bakeries that specialize in those or ask the vendor directly.
3. **Read reviews** – Look at recent customer photos and comments on Google, Yelp, or the platform’s own review system.
4. **Ask about delivery** – Some bakeries only do local delivery; others ship nationwide (Goldbelly). Confirm delivery time windows and any special handling instructions.
5. **Plan ahead** – For big events (weddings, birthdays), place orders 2–4 weeks in advance. For last‑minute needs, use same‑day delivery services or local pickup.

---

#### Quick starter list (U.S. examples)

| City | Bakery | Specialty |
|------|--------|-----------|
| New York | Levain Bakery | Classic chocolate chip & custom cakes |
| Los Angeles | Baked by Melissa | Bite‑size cupcakes, vegan options |
| Chicago | Magnolia Bakery | Traditional & seasonal flavors |
| Austin | Sweet Tooth | Gluten‑free & keto-friendly |
| Seattle | The Sweet Spot | Vegan & dairy‑free cakes |

If you let me know your city or any specific dietary preferences, I can narrow down the best local spots for you!
